claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations and distinct phase boundaries.
A transformer model can reliably predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
A modest, strategically augmented set of in situ tensile and fracture data is sufficient to train the proposed model.
Transformer self-attention can capture complex relationships and assign differing importance to alloy constituents.
Pre-training on broad materials data followed by fine-tuning on HEA data mitigates data scarcity and improves generalization.
Synchronizing diffraction and DIC during testing captures dynamic microstructural evolution relevant to mechanical behavior.
Multilevel chemical fluctuations and phase-boundary features activate during deformation.
These chemical fluctuations and phase boundaries govern elastic and plastic responses in HfNbTiVAl10.
These heterostructural features govern crack initiation and propagation.
Self-attention will learn the relative influence of localized microstructural heterogeneities on elastic and plastic responses.
Data augmentation will ensure robust model calibration against measurement noise.
The proposed model will integrate real-time microstructural changes with mechanical behavior.
Transformer models have shown higher predictive accuracy than random forests and Gaussian processes for HEA elongation and ultimate tensile strength.
The proposed approach will reduce prediction error by about 50% relative to conventional machine-learning or first-principles methods.
The proposed approach will reduce computational and analysis time by approximately two orders of magnitude.
CALPHAD, first-principles, and brute-force simulation methods are computationally intensive and provide less reliable toughness predictions.
Poor synchronization, excessive noise, or diffraction–DIC misalignment may make the model unreliable.
Transfer learning may fail when source HEA data do not represent microstructural peculiarities unique to HfNbTiVAl10.
The model will be prospectively evaluated on blinded HfNbTiVAl10 samples using measured Young’s modulus, yield strength, fracture toughness, and prediction time.
Failure to achieve at least a 50% error reduction or an approximately 100-fold time reduction will falsify the hypothesis.
